Portfolio news brief — 16 September 2026

Market and major-name developments
- The 10-year Treasury note yield moved above the key 5% mark after a Federal Reserve rate increase and comments from Chairman Kevin Warsh highlighting persistent inflation risks. The benchmark yield was up 2 basis points at 5.016%. (CNBC)
- The Federal Reserve on Wednesday approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years and indicated another is to come, as part of an effort aimed at combating inflation brought on by spiraling oil prices and other factors. In a move that markets widely anticipated , the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee voted 12-0 to increase its key interest rate by a quarter percentage point, or 25 basis points. (CNBC)
- Harris Financial’s Jamie Cox, Raymond James’s Larry Adam, JPMorgan’s David Kelly, RBC’s Francis Donald and Yardeni Research's Ed Yardeni discuss the latest Federal Reserve decision. (CNBC)
- CNBC's Steve Liesman reports on news regarding the Federal Reserve. (CNBC)
- Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh answers questions following the central bank's decision to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points. (CNBC)

Costco (COST)
- Uber Eats partnership to 47 states from availability in 17 states, according to a Wednesday press release . With the expansion, nearly 600 Costco locations will be available for delivery on Uber Eats for members of the warehouse club. (CNBC)

Meta (META)
- Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg shared his view of artificial intelligence safety on Tuesday, taking a stance that's more akin to the perspective of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang rather than Anthropic chief Dario Amodei. Zuckerberg said in a post on X and other social media platforms that he believes AI labs that fail to "focus on alignment will fall behind," referring to the kind of work that developers conduct to ensure the technologies adhere to human values. (CNBC)

SanDisk (SNDK)
- Micron and Sandisk have been two of the most defining AI stocks over the past year. The shifting focus from AI chips to memory chips produced tremendous returns for early investors, and people who missed out on those two growth stocks are eying new opportunities. (The Motley Fool)

NVIDIA (NVDA; VOO top-five holding)
- Nvidia ( NVDA +0.81% ) remains the dominant supplier of graphics processing units (GPUs) used to train and run artificial intelligence (AI) models. However, its latest acquisition suggests the company also wants a stronger position in how developers choose and deploy those models. (The Motley Fool)
- Nvidia ( NVDA +0.81% ) , the world's largest company by market cap, isn't showing any signs of slowing down thanks to the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom. The company's revenue more than doubled in the previous quarter to $96.2 billion, accelerating from the year-ago period's growth rate of 56%. (The Motley Fool)
- AI factories are the infrastructure of the intelligence era. Scaling them responsibly will depend as much on innovation across the grid as inside the data center. (NVIDIA official news)
- Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. (NVIDIA official news)

Bitcoin (BTC)
- The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by a quarter point Wednesday, its first hike since 2023, lifting the federal funds rate to a target range of 3.75% to 4% from 3.50% to 3.75%. Bitcoin remained flat in the minutes before and after the announcement, swinging between $75,00 and $75,800. (Decrypt)
- The software that lets users independently verify Bitcoin payments is getting an update aimed at speeding up those checks and fixing security flaws, with a release targeted for October. Bitcoin Core 32.0 entered release-candidate testing on Monday, according to the project’s schedule . (Decrypt)

Ethereum (ETH)
- Nikhil Chandhok, Chief Technology and Product Officer at Circle, joins CoinDesk Contributor Kate Irwin on Markets Outlook the day Arc mainnet goes live. Plus, Beezie Founder and CEO Andrea Miele on why tokenized luxury goods are the next frontier for provenance and liquidity. (CoinDesk)
- Crypto traders holding long, or bullish, futures bets have taken a sharp hit over the past 24 hours after the Clarity Act failed a Senate procedural vote. Exchanges liquidated about $571 million in long positions in that window, the highest tally since Aug. (CoinDesk)

USD Coin (USDC)
- Circle has switched on Arc, a Layer 1 blockchain built for payments, trading and “agentic economic activity,” announcing the public mainnet on Wednesday. Chief executive Jeremy Allaire called it "the single most significant launch in Circle's history since USDC itself," in a press release. (Decrypt)
- Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire joins 'Squawk Box' to discuss the fate of the Clarity Act after it failed to pass a procedural vote in the Senate, what's next for the crypto industry, and more. (CNBC)

AbbVie (ABBV; XLV top-five holding)
- Dividend Kings are arguably among the best income stocks on the planet. These are corporations that have raised their payouts for at least 50 consecutive years. (The Motley Fool)

Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO)
- More and more investors of all stripes are pouring into exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and the tape tells that tale. Goldman Sachs recently noted that in the first six months of 2026, more than $1 trillion flowed into ETFs trading in the U.S., putting the industry on pace for north of $2 trillion in annual inflows this year. (The Motley Fool)

Informational only — verify primary sources before making investment decisions.
Routine price moves and stock-picking speculation are intentionally excluded.
